node_kinds.name: GH_Enterprise
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Enterprise account that contains organizations, enterprise teams, roles, and managed users

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub Enterprise account. This is the top-level container for enterprise organizations, enterprise teams, enterprise roles, managed users, runner groups, and enterprise SAML configuration.

node_kinds.name: GH_EnterpriseTeam
node_kinds.description: A team managed at the GitHub Enterprise level and assignable across organizations

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents an enterprise-managed team that can be assigned into one or more organizations. Enterprise teams can carry enterprise roles and project into organization teams that inherit their membership.

node_kinds.name: GH_EnterpriseRole
node_kinds.description: The role a user or team has at the GitHub Enterprise level

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a built-in or custom enterprise role. Enterprise roles are assigned directly to users or to enterprise teams and carry enterprise-wide permissions such as managing enterprise admins, members, or organization admins.

node_kinds.name: GH_EnterpriseManagedUser
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Enterprise managed user account linked to an enterprise identity provider

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub Enterprise Managed User account. The node preserves the enterprise-level account record and maps it to the backing `GH_User` used elsewhere in the graph.

node_kinds.name: GH_Organization
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Organization—top-level container for repositories, teams, and settings

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub organization. This is the root node of the organization graph and serves as the primary container for repositories, roles, runner groups, credentials, and security settings.

Organization-level settings such as default repository permissions, Actions configuration, and security features are captured as properties on this node.

node_kinds.name: GH_User
node_kinds.description: An individual GitHub user account

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub user who is a member of the organization. Users are associated with organization roles and can be assigned to repository roles and team roles.

node_kinds.name: GH_Team
node_kinds.description: A team within an organization, grouping users for shared access and collaboration

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub team within an organization. Teams can contain members and maintainers, inherit membership through parent-child team relationships, and receive repository or organization roles that grant downstream access.

node_kinds.name: GH_Repository
node_kinds.description: A code repository in an organization, containing files, issues, and other resources

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub repository within the organization. Repository nodes capture metadata about the repo including visibility, Actions enablement status, and security configuration. Repository role nodes are created alongside each repository to represent the permission levels available.

For repositories with active workflows, the collector records the applicable default workflow permissions and whether workflows may approve pull request reviews. These properties preserve the repository-level policy input later used to derive effective GITHUB_TOKEN permissions for workflow jobs.

The `branch_count`, `environment_count`, and `deploy_key_count` properties preserve GitHub-reported totals that can be compared to collected child nodes to identify incomplete collection before relying on branch-, environment-, or deploy-key-dependent analysis.

node_kinds.name: GH_Branch
node_kinds.description: A named reference in a repository representing a line of development

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a Git branch within a repository. Branch nodes capture basic branch information and whether the branch is protected. Protection rule details are stored separately on `GH_BranchProtectionRule` nodes, while post-processed `GH_CanWriteBranch` edges summarize who can effectively write the branch.

node_kinds.name: GH_BranchProtectionRule
node_kinds.description: A branch protection rule that applies to one or more branches via pattern matching

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a branch protection rule configured on a GitHub repository. Protection rules define requirements that must be met before changes can be merged to matching branches, including review gates, status checks, and push restrictions.

A single protection rule can apply to multiple branches through pattern matching.

node_kinds.name: GH_OrgRole
node_kinds.description: The role a user has at the organization level (e.g., admin, member)

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents an organization-level role such as Owner, Member, or a custom organization role. Organization roles define what permissions users and teams have at the organization level and may also inherit repository-wide base roles.

node_kinds.name: GH_TeamRole
node_kinds.description: The role a user has within a team (e.g., maintainer, member)

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a role within a GitHub team. Team roles connect users to organization or enterprise teams and transitively to repository roles assigned to those teams.

node_kinds.name: GH_RepoRole
node_kinds.description: The permission granted to a user or team on a repository (e.g., admin, write, read)

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a repository-level permission role. Each repository has default roles such as Read, Write, Admin, Triage, and Maintain, plus any applicable custom roles. These roles are the bridge between users or teams and the repository, branches, environments, and security data they can affect.

node_kinds.name: GH_Workflow
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Actions workflow defined in a repository

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub Actions workflow defined in a repository. Workflow nodes capture the workflow definition metadata including its file path, state, containing repository, and the full YAML contents of the workflow file. Only repositories with GitHub Actions enabled are queried for workflows.

When present, `workflow_permissions` captures the top-level `permissions` declaration from the workflow YAML.

node_kinds.name: GH_WorkflowJob
node_kinds.description: A job within a GitHub Actions workflow, with a runner, permissions, and an ordered list of steps

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a single job within a GitHub Actions workflow. Jobs are the top-level execution units of a workflow: they run on a runner, hold a set of steps, and can declare permissions, environments, and dependencies on other jobs.

When the job has a statically resolvable self-hosted `runs-on` selector, `GH_RunsOn` edges identify each runner that currently satisfies the declared label and runner-group constraints under the repository's runner access policy. These edges represent schedulability, not historical execution.

When present, `job_permissions` captures the job-level `permissions` declaration from the workflow YAML. `effective_github_token_permissions` captures the calculated static `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions after applying the repository default, workflow-level declaration, and job-level declaration.

`GH_CanAccessSecret` edges identify secrets statically referenced by the job's modeled steps or job-level `env` block that the job execution context can access. `GH_CanInterceptJob` edges from runners not explicitly marked ephemeral identify jobs whose future execution context may be exposed if that runner is controlled. When a job targets an environment and its effective permissions include `id-token:write`, `GH_CanRequestOIDCTokenFor` identifies a static upper-bound OIDC capability for that environment. Runtime permission recalculation, such as forked `pull_request` permission downgrades, may prevent a specific execution from requesting OIDC even when this edge exists.

When `runs_on_is_dynamic` is true, runner matching and interception status remain unresolved. The collector does not emit `GH_CanInterceptJob` edges for the job, so the absence of an edge must not be treated as evidence that the job is definitively non-interceptable.

node_kinds.name: GH_WorkflowStep
node_kinds.description: A single step within a GitHub Actions job — either a uses: action reference or a run: shell command

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a single step within a GitHub Actions job. A step is either a `uses:` action reference or a `run:` shell command. Steps are the leaf nodes of the workflow execution tree and are the primary location where secrets and variables are consumed.

node_kinds.name: GH_Environment
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Actions deployment environment with protection rules and deployment branch policies

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub Actions deployment environment configured on a repository. Environments can have protection rules including required reviewers, wait timers, administrator bypass behavior, and deployment branch policies.

Repositories always contain their environments. When custom branch policies are configured, the environment also contains one or more environment branch policy nodes that describe which branches are allowed to deploy. Environment-scoped secrets and variables are modeled as child nodes of the environment and become available to workflow jobs that reference it.

`GH_CanRequestOIDCTokenFor` edges from workflow jobs identify jobs with a static upper-bound capability to request a GitHub-signed OIDC token for this environment because their effective `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions include `id-token:write`. Runtime permission recalculation, such as forked `pull_request` permission downgrades, may prevent a specific execution from requesting OIDC even when this edge exists.

node_kinds.name: GH_EnvironmentBranchPolicy
node_kinds.description: A deployment branch policy attached to a GitHub environment, such as an exact branch name or wildcard pattern like release/*

node_kinds.name: GH_OrgSecret
node_kinds.description: An organization-level GitHub Actions secret that can be scoped to all, private, or selected repositories

node_kinds.name: GH_RepoSecret
node_kinds.description: A repository-level GitHub Actions secret accessible only to workflows in that repository

node_kinds.name: GH_EnvironmentSecret
node_kinds.description: An environment-level GitHub Actions secret scoped to a specific deployment environment

node_kinds.name: GH_OrgVariable
node_kinds.description: An organization-level GitHub Actions variable that can be scoped to all, private, or selected repositories. Unlike secrets, variable values are readable.

node_kinds.name: GH_RepoVariable
node_kinds.description: A repository-level GitHub Actions variable accessible only to workflows in that repository. Unlike secrets, variable values are readable.

node_kinds.name: GH_DeployKey
node_kinds.description: A repository-scoped SSH deploy key that grants read-only or read-write access to repository contents

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a repository-scoped SSH deploy key that grants read-only or read-write access to repository contents. Deploy keys are linked to their containing repository and, when GitHub exposes the actor, the user who added them.

node_kinds.name: GH_Secret
node_kinds.description: Generic label applied to GitHub secret nodes across organization, repository, and environment scope

markdown.content:
## Overview

Generic label applied to GitHub Actions secret nodes across organization, repository, and environment scope. Concrete secret kinds inherit this navigation so analysts can see where a secret is scoped, which repositories can receive it, and which workflow jobs can access it.

node_kinds.name: GH_Variable
node_kinds.description: Generic label applied to GitHub variable nodes across organization, repository, and environment scope

markdown.content:
## Overview

Generic label applied to GitHub Actions variable nodes across organization, repository, and environment scope. Unlike secrets, variable values are readable, but their scope and workflow usage are still useful when reviewing execution context.

node_kinds.name: GH_RunnerGroup
node_kinds.description: Generic label applied to GitHub self-hosted runner group nodes across enterprise and organization scope

markdown.content:
## Overview

Generic label applied to GitHub self-hosted runner group nodes across enterprise and organization scope. Runner groups control which repositories and workflows may dispatch jobs to their contained runners.

node_kinds.name: GH_Runner
node_kinds.description: Generic label applied to GitHub self-hosted runner nodes across enterprise, organization, and repository scope

markdown.content:
## Overview

Generic label applied to GitHub self-hosted runner nodes across enterprise, organization, and repository scope.

A runner may be eligible for one or more workflow jobs through static `runs-on` resolution. Persistent runners that are not explicitly marked ephemeral may also receive `GH_CanInterceptJob` edges to jobs whose future execution context could be exposed if the runner is controlled.

node_kinds.name: GH_EnterpriseRunnerGroup
node_kinds.description: An enterprise-scoped GitHub self-hosted runner group that controls runner access and visibility

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a self-hosted runner group owned by a GitHub Enterprise account. Enterprise runner groups contain enterprise runners directly and are projected into organizations through inherited `GH_OrgRunnerGroup` nodes. Repositories and branches reach the enterprise runners through those organization-facing projections rather than directly through the enterprise group.

node_kinds.name: GH_OrgRunnerGroup
node_kinds.description: An organization-scoped GitHub self-hosted runner group that controls runner access and visibility

node_kinds.name: GH_EnterpriseRunner
node_kinds.description: An enterprise-scoped GitHub self-hosted runner available to organizations through enterprise runner groups

node_kinds.name: GH_OrgRunner
node_kinds.description: An organization-scoped GitHub self-hosted runner available to selected repositories or workflows

node_kinds.name: GH_RepoRunner
node_kinds.description: A repository-scoped GitHub self-hosted runner available to jobs in a single repository

node_kinds.name: GH_EnvironmentVariable
node_kinds.description: An environment-level GitHub Actions variable scoped to a specific deployment environment. Unlike secrets, variable values are readable.

node_kinds.name: GH_SecretScanningAlert
node_kinds.description: A GitHub Advanced Security alert indicating a secret was accidentally committed to a repository

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub secret scanning alert detected in a repository. Alerts capture the secret type, validity status, and resolution state. When a leaked GitHub token can be mapped back to a collected user, a traversable `GH_ValidToken` edge records the compromise path.

node_kinds.name: GH_SamlIdentityProvider
node_kinds.description: A SAML identity provider configured for the organization, enabling SSO

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a SAML identity provider configured for a GitHub organization or enterprise. It captures the SSO configuration and serves as the parent container for external identity mappings back to GitHub users.

node_kinds.name: GH_ExternalIdentity
node_kinds.description: An external identity from a SAML/SCIM provider linked to a GitHub user for SSO authentication

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents an external identity from a SAML or SCIM identity provider that is linked to a GitHub user. This node preserves the identity-provider attributes used to understand how a corporate identity maps into GitHub.

node_kinds.name: GH_App
node_kinds.description: A GitHub App definition representing the registered application. The app owner controls the private key used to generate installation tokens.

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub App definition. The app owner controls the private key used to generate installation tokens for every installation of this app, so compromise of the app can affect every organization where it is installed.

node_kinds.name: GH_AppInstallation
node_kinds.description: A GitHub App installed on the organization with specific permissions and repository access

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a GitHub App installed on an organization. Installations have a permission set and repository scope, and are linked back to the parent `GH_App` that owns the private key used to mint installation tokens.

node_kinds.name: GH_PersonalAccessToken
node_kinds.description: A fine-grained personal access token granted access to organization resources

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a fine-grained personal access token that has been granted access to organization resources. The token is linked to its owner, the organization that approved it, and the repositories it can access.

node_kinds.name: GH_PersonalAccessTokenRequest
node_kinds.description: A pending request from an organization member to access organization resources with a fine-grained personal access token

markdown.content:
## Overview

Represents a pending request from an organization member to access organization resources with a fine-grained personal access token. Requested permissions are stored on the node, but no access edges are projected until GitHub reports an approved token.

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanEditProtection

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanReadSecret
relationship_kinds.description: Org role can read an organization secret by creating a repository in scope

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanReadSecretScanningAlert
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Role can read secret scanning alerts (computed from GH_ViewSecretScanningAlerts permission + GH_Contains)

relationship_kinds.name: GH_ProtectedBy

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasSecret

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasVariable

relationship_kinds.name: GH_ValidToken

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasSamlIdentityProvider

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasExternalIdentity

relationship_kinds.name: GH_MapsToUser

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasPersonalAccessToken

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasPersonalAccessTokenRequest

relationship_kinds.name: GH_InstalledAs

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanAccess

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanUseRunner

relationship_kinds.name: GH_IsEligibleFor

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanWriteBranch
relationship_kinds.description: [Repository - Computed] Role can push to this branch after evaluating branch protection rules, push restrictions, and bypass allowances

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanCreateBranch
relationship_kinds.description: [Repository - Computed] Role can create new branches in this repository (unprotected branches that bypass the merge gate)

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanCreateEnvironment
relationship_kinds.description: Repo role can create new GitHub environments in this repository by editing a workflow that references a nonexistent environment name

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanEditEnvironment

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanAssumeIdentity

relationship_kinds.name: GH_SyncedTo
relationship_kinds.description: External identity (Azure, Okta, PingOne) is synced to this GitHub user via SSO/SCIM

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CallsWorkflow
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job calls a reusable workflow — GH_WorkflowJob → GH_Workflow

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanPwnRequest
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Repo role can exploit a pwn-requestable workflow to execute arbitrary code with the target's secrets and permissions — GH_RepoRole → GH_Repository / GH_Branch

relationship_kinds.name: GH_DependsOn
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job must run after another job (needs: dependency) — ordering only, not an access path

relationship_kinds.name: GH_DeploysTo
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job deploys to a GitHub Environment — GH_WorkflowJob → GH_Environment

relationship_kinds.name: GH_RunsOn
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job can be scheduled on this self-hosted runner based on its static runs-on selector — GH_WorkflowJob → GH_Runner

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanInterceptJob
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Persistent self-hosted runner can intercept a workflow job that may be scheduled on it — GH_Runner → GH_WorkflowJob

relationship_kinds.name: GH_HasMember
relationship_kinds.description: Enterprise or organization has this user as a member

relationship_kinds.name: GH_UsesSecret
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job or step references a secret by name — GH_WorkflowJob / GH_WorkflowStep → GH_RepoSecret / GH_OrgSecret / GH_EnvironmentSecret (scope match)

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanAccessSecret
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Workflow job execution context can access a statically referenced secret — GH_WorkflowJob → GH_RepoSecret / GH_OrgSecret / GH_EnvironmentSecret

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanRequestOIDCTokenFor
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Workflow job has a static upper-bound capability to request a GitHub OIDC token for its deployment environment — GH_WorkflowJob → GH_Environment

relationship_kinds.name: GH_UsesVariable
relationship_kinds.description: [Workflow] Job or step references a variable by name — GH_WorkflowJob / GH_WorkflowStep → GH_RepoVariable / GH_OrgVariable / GH_EnvironmentVariable (scope match)

relationship_kinds.name: GH_CanDeployToEnvironment
relationship_kinds.description: [Computed] Repository, branch, repo role, or reviewer can deploy to this GitHub environment after evaluating deployment branch policy, reviewer gates, and admin bypass behavior; reviewer edges require both self-approval and a deployable code path

relationship_kinds.name: GH_MatchesEnvironmentPolicy
